# Your results

Everything Mini-Me produces in a conversation is collected in the **Pinboard**, the panel on the
right side of the window. This chapter explains each part of it.

![The Pinboard](images/results-pinboard.png)

## Plan

For bigger questions, Mini-Me writes a short **checklist** of what it is going to do. The step
it is working on is highlighted, finished steps fade, and steps still to come are listed
below. The plan stays after the answer is finished, so you can see what was done.

## Background Jobs

Some tasks take several minutes (for example generating hypotheses or analysing a large
dataset). These appear under **Background Jobs** while they run, so you can keep asking other
questions in the meantime.

- A job that says **waiting for your approval** or **waiting for your input** needs you —
  click it and answer. See [Approvals and credits](approvals.qmd).
- If a job finishes while you are in another conversation, a message tells you it
  **finished while you were away**. Click **open it** to see the results.

## Files

The **Files** section shows everything saved in this conversation's folder: charts, cleaned
data, tables, notebooks, reports and the files you attached.

- **Click a file** to preview it inside Mini-Me. Charts and images open full size; use the
  arrows to move between them.
- Choose **open outside** to open the file in its normal program (for example Excel).
- To see all files in Windows File Explorer, open the conversation's folder (see
  [Where your files are saved](projects.qmd#where-your-files-are-saved)).

![Previewing a chart](images/results-file-preview.png)

::: {.callout-tip title="Files saved in the wrong place?"}
Sometimes a task saves a file outside the conversation's folder. When that happens, Mini-Me
offers a button like **Copy 2 files into this conversation** so nothing gets lost.
:::

## Sources

**Sources** lists the papers and references used in the answers. Click a source to open it in
your browser. When there are many, click **View More** to see the full list.

::: {.callout-warning title="Always check references"}
Most references come from a real search, but a few may have been written by the AI from memory.
The Sources list tells you how many of them **"came from the model rather than from a search"**
— check those carefully before you cite them.
:::

![The Sources list](images/results-sources.png)

## Datasets

When the **Dataverse Explorer** finds datasets, it lists them in its answer with their title,
a short description and a link to their page in the CIP Dataverse. Click a link to open the
dataset's page in your browser.

To work with a dataset, ask for it — for example *"Download the second dataset and profile
it"*. Only **public** datasets can be downloaded; for restricted ones, use the dataset's page to
request access from CIP.

## Your PDFs

When you give Mini-Me PDF files, the **PDF Librarian** reads them and keeps them in this
conversation's library. The PDFs themselves are listed under **Files**.

To search inside your PDFs, just ask — for example *"Which of my PDFs discuss frost
damage?"*. Mini-Me searches **by meaning**, so it finds relevant passages even if they don't use
your exact words.

## Reports

Ask *"Write a report of what we found"* and the **Report Writer** creates a full report with
methods, findings, limitations and references. It appears under **Files**.

**To save the report as a PDF:** press **`Ctrl+P`** and choose
**Save the latest report as a PDF**. The PDF is saved in the conversation's folder.

![A report saved as PDF](images/results-report-pdf.png)

## How was this made? (provenance)

To see **which specialists worked on this conversation, and in what order**, press
**`Ctrl+P`** and choose **Show this conversation's provenance**.

You can view it as a **timeline** (what happened, step by step) or as a **graph** (who passed
work to whom). Use **Save as SVG** to keep a picture of it, for example for a methods section.

![The provenance view](images/results-provenance.png)
